description: The establishments in Luxembourg that fall under the EU Seveso III Directive on major accident hazards involving dangerous substances. The data.public.lu entry says Luxembourg reported them under Directive 2012/18/EU in two classes, currently 9 lower-tier and 9 upper-tier establishments, with the Inspection du Travail et des Mines responsible for inspection; it is published as an INSPIRE production facilities layer, downloadable as GML (updated 29 July 2026) and as a WMS view service, free under CC0. A separate list of Seveso establishments from January 2020 is downloadable as XLSX under CC0, and a 2018 map of the Greater Region from SIG-GR (CC BY) gives Seveso establishments per municipality, nuclear power plant emergency zones and CORINE artificial surfaces as GeoJSON and shapefiles. Coverage is Luxembourg (and the Greater Region for the 2018 map). Caveats: a small set of sites, and the 2018 cross-border map is not updated. For simulation it places the country's major-hazard chemical sites, to model accident zones around them and their exposure to river floods. Related catalogue records include eSPIRS and eMARS.
